deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous page. M is a small category whose objects D_n are indexed by an ordered set (written as a barred N; the next page calls it 'ens. ordonné', so it is not necessarily the natural numbers). For each n:
- J_n is the ordered set of subobjects of D_n.
- τ_n : J_n → N is a strictly increasing 'type' map with image N_{≤n}.
- J_n has a largest element d_n, and τ_n^{-1}(n) = {d_n}.
- For n' ≤ n, the map u ↦ u(d_{n'}) identifies Hom(D_{n'}, D_n) with J_{n,n'} := τ_n^{-1}(n'), the elements of type n'. This gives an injection ρ_{n,n'} : J_{n,n'} → Hom(J_{n'}, J_n), ξ ↦ u^n_ξ.

This page:
(1) States the properties of u_ξ. We have u_ξ(d_{n'}) = ξ. Moreover u_ξ is an order isomorphism J_{n'} ≅ (J_n)_{≤ξ}: the subobjects of D_{n'} correspond to the subobjects of D_n contained in the image ξ, because all maps are monomorphisms. For n' = n, J_{n,n} = {d_n} and u_{d_n} = id.
(2) Claims that the data (N, (J_n), (τ_n), (ρ_{n,n'})) recover M up to equivalence, once one adds a compatibility condition saying how the 'standard' maps compose. For n'' ≤ n' ≤ n, η ∈ J_{n',n''} and ξ ∈ J_{n,n'}, one needs u^n_ξ ∘ u^{n'}_η = u^n_ζ with ζ = u^n_ξ(η) = (u^n_ξ u^{n'}_η)(d_{n''}). This expresses that 'admissible' maps J_{n'} → J_n (those of the form u_ξ) are closed under composition.
(3) Defines the category M_0. Its objects are N. Hom_{M_0}(n', n) is empty if n' ≰ n, and is the set of admissible maps J_{n'} → J_n if n' ≤ n. Composition is composition of maps.

The next page states that the canonical functor M → M_0 is an equivalence, and an isomorphism when M is reduced (skeletal). It then begins axiomatizing such data abstractly.

In modern terms, M is a category in which:
- every morphism is a monomorphism;
- every object has trivial automorphism group;
- there are no non-identity endomorphisms (the type map is strictly increasing);
- every slice M/D_n is a poset with a top element.
M is thus a skeletal direct category with poset slices, i.e. a category of 'regular cells'. Examples are the semi-simplicial category Δ_inj, face maps of globes, and face categories of regular CW or polyhedral complexes. Grothendieck is giving a combinatorial presentation of such a category by its family of face posets, each closed under principal down-sets. This is the familiar idea that such a category is determined by its 'cell shapes' and the down-set isomorphisms. The archive context ('Champs 1') suggests this serves to describe a category of models or shapes, probably for presheaves or stacks over it.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The composition condition is correctly formulated: u_ξ u_η sends d_{n''} to u_ξ(η), and maps are determined by the image of the top element.
Notation drifts between J_n/I_n and T_n/τ_n across pages.
On the next page the composition axiom is miswritten as u^{n'}_ξ ∘ u^{n'}_η; it should be u^n_ξ ∘ u^{n'}_η.

Implicit assumption: that M → M_0 is fully faithful requires ρ injective and that Hom determines the image map. This was established on the previous page via the bijection Hom(D_{n'}, D_n) ≅ τ_n^{-1}(n'), which presupposes monomorphisms with trivial automorphisms of subobjects.

ideas.what: Encoding a category of monomorphisms via the posets of subobjects of each object, with a strictly increasing 'type' (dimension) map, and the identification Hom(D_{n'}, D_n) ≅ elements of type n'.
ideas.modern_name: Direct (Reedy) category with poset slices / regular skeletal category; face posets with degree function
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; direct categories with degree functions are in Reedy-category theory (Reedy 1970s, Hovey). Regular/elegant variants appear in Bergner–Rezk.
ideas.where_published: Possibly related remarks on 'modelizers' and test categories in Pursuing Stacks, but this explicit axiomatization is not known to me there.

ideas.what: Each principal down-set (J_n)_{≤ξ} is isomorphic to J_{τ(ξ)} via the map u_ξ, together with a cocycle-like composition condition u_ξ u_η = u_{u_ξ(η)}.
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of a category with poset slices from its slice posets (each slice M/x ≅ face poset of x)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (e.g. 'cellular' or 'regular' categories in combinatorial topology)

ideas.what: Reconstruction of M up to equivalence (isomorphism if skeletal) as the category M_0 of 'admissible' maps between the subobject posets.
ideas.modern_name: Embedding of a direct category with poset slices into Poset via x ↦ M/x

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, correct combinatorial encoding of a skeletal direct category with poset slices (face posets plus degree map). This is standard folklore, and the page only sets up axioms that continue on the next page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 should read roughly: 'i.e. on a, pour ξ ∈ J_{n,n'} (i.e. x ∈ J_n, τ_n(x) = n'), u_ξ(d_{n'}) = ξ'.
'De plus, ξ fixé arbitraire[?], on a: u_ξ induit un isom J_{n'} → (J_n)_{≤ξ}'. The phrase 'un pr[?]' is likely 'arbitraire' or similar, and 'iso' is 'isom'.
'reconstituer la catégorie M, à équivalence près; il manque encore une condition' — 'où' should be 'à'.
'(ρ_{n,n'})_{(n',n) ∈ N×N, n' ≤ n}' — the index carries the underscript n' ≤ n.
The indexing set is a barred/crossed N, apparently an arbitrary ordered set rather than the natural numbers (cf. next page: 'ens. ordonné').
'ζ = u^n_ξ(η)': the transcription's ζ is correct; the subscript in u^n_ζ was overwritten in the manuscript.
J_n is written with a script J; 'I_n' in the transcription is the same object.
